facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 水_食神 (Water carrying The Artisan). Persona The Artisan (食神). Definition line: "Output that flows from you, giving that feels like being". Keyword Flow, charge gentle, poles catalyst Grace / friction Coasting. Family function: Expression. Cost dimension: giving that feels like being; worth tangled with what is made. Arena: craft, hands, the table, warmth of making, fed and feeding. Classical portrait: ease and appetite; output that flows without assertion; generous, content, prone to drift and indulgence. Ruled domains: Expression, Enjoyment, Children. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 伤官.
Element arena: Water (depth, current, tide, rain, spring, flow). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Metal. structural_interaction seed: "Metal generating Water same-polarity — precision as natural source of flowing depth".
- k2_overview: "Your Water moves as the Artisan: a spring that feeds everything downstream. Your output flows, words, ideas, comfort, care, without visible effort, and people drink from it more than you notice. You nourish by permeating: the right thing said gently, the mood eased, the story that waters a dry week."
- k2_functional: "Your expression pours: fluent, warm, endlessly refilled. Writing and talk both come as flow."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Fluent","Nourishing","Easygoing"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Expression":"Your expression is the stream itself: writing, conversation, comfort flowing daily. Volume is natural to you, so add channels: publish, record, send. Water that reaches others is what turns gift to harvest.","Enjoyment":"You enjoy in gentle currents: long baths, slow music, conversation into the night. Honor these as necessities. A spring that is never let pool goes brackish.","Children":"With the young you nourish invisibly: the listening, the softening, the words that raise them without their noticing. They will quote you for life, usually without knowing whom they are quoting."}
- fn_reading.friction.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.friction; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 水_伤官 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Silver-tongued","Inspired","Free-flowing"],"friction":["Toxic","Mocking","Uncontainable"]}
- Sibling cell 水_伤官 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Your words work on people the way water works on iron, slowly, invisibly, and completely. The little digs, the accurate observations shared at the wrong moment, the humor with acid in it: nothing dramatic, ever. Just gradual damage that everyone attributes to time."

Core element Metal, energy element Water. Law: Metal feeds Water (金生水: dew beads on the cold blade). Relative to the core the energy is the fed, so Water is this core's Expression. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Metal core that shows Water on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Water as the Expression is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 金_水's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Drifting along is easier than steering, and mostly you do. More Water moves through you than comes back in, so you drift with what moves instead of picking a direction. You end up where the day takes you, rarely where you meant to go.

value_b.text: Whatever is already moving is where you drift, because drifting costs less than deciding. You drift with someone's plan rather than make your own, so you end the week with no choice to name. Remember you were allowed to want more than the drift.

value.text: Most days you drift, and it rarely feels like a loss. Since you take in less than you let out, you drift to whatever is nearest rather than pick. You still want things, and the drift costs you each one that was not nearby.

value.text: Going with the drift keeps things easy for everyone. Whenever you drift with a plan in place of saying what you wanted, you leave the people closest to you guessing. You hand them a maybe where they needed a real answer.

value.text: Putting comfort ahead of the plan is how most evenings go. What you pour out all day leaves you emptier than you admit, so you take the comfort before anything is done. You enjoy the comfort less while the job sits undone.

value_b.text: Comfort beats finishing the thing whenever you let the two compete. You want comfort now more than you want to feel done later, because comfort never makes you wait. Bear in mind that comfortable comes around more often than finished does, and only finished lasts.

value.text: Whenever the day gets hard, you put comfort first and the hard part second. You comfort yourself rather than sit with it, while what you avoided waits for you unchanged. Remember that what you were after all along was rest.

value.text: Keeping everyone around you comfortable comes before asking anything of them. Since you put a child's comfort ahead of what they promised, you take from them the small steadiness they needed. You spare them the promise and the pride of seeing it through.

value.text: What you have, you give away before checking whether enough is left. Since giving is the nearest you get to feeling like yourself, you give away more than you keep. You are one of the people you give to, and that is worth remembering.

value_b.text: Giving it away is your first reflex and your last defence. You give it away rather than be caught keeping it, so you give your time away before choosing where. Keep some of what you make, since you were never required to give it all.

value.text: Giving things away is quicker for you than working out what you need. Giving out more than comes back, you end most weeks with less than you started with. You go without exactly what you gave away, the rest and the money.

value.text: You give your hours to whoever is nearest, without deciding. Whenever you give everyone something rather than save enough for the few counting on you, you leave them less than was theirs. You give away to everyone the hours meant for the few.
